parsed.explanation: Combined regime is High-to-Elevated Risk. Entry: the national foreign ministry refuses or blocks non-matching sex markers, and the 24 Feb 2025 cable allows refusal on any document discrepancy and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility. Custody: documented immigration-custody forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse, plus national corrections policy harms. Facilities: birth-sex bans in state government buildings, school bans, and a documented trespass arrest. Minors and guardians: care is criminalised under 19 and national enforcement threats reach adults. Violence is undocumented because the 3.8/100k figure is an undercount floor. Hate-crime coverage is partial, and no statewide protection exists. Enforcement is ongoing and partly enjoined.

entry_documents.exposure: Foreign ministry stopped non-M/F markers and mismatched sex markers; passports confiscated or blocked, travellers stranded; cable refuses cases on any discrepancy; possible permanent fraud-ground ineligibility (not automatic).
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; national civil-liberties suit pending; Supreme Court allowed restrictions to take effect.
entry_documents.interaction: Document refusal at entry can escalate to fraud finding, detention or stranding; a visitor's home passport governs, so mismatch exposure depends on the traveller's own documents.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of transgender men reported. Subpoenas of hospital records for under-19s; threatened prosecution of teachers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Documented litigation and some injunctions; no documented operative custody protection for visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy can lead to immigration detention; custody conditions carry documented harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Birth-sex facility bans in government buildings including schools and colleges; criminal trespass for willful entry plus refusal to depart in some states; one first-known trespass arrest (handcuffed, 24h held in men's ward) at a state capitol; bans reach some private settings in 6 states; state bathroom law extended to campuses per a third-party assessment, enactment status unverified.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Statutory exemptions (emergency, chaperoning minors, custodial purposes) exist on paper; no statewide public-accommodation protection in this state.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility rules are universal-exposure measures. The national frame's birth-sex custody and facility rules layer onto state bans. Trespass arrests follow from ordinary facility use.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care under 19 (felony, enforced since 2023). Proposed national rules would bar public insurance reimbursement for under-18 care. Care denial for accompanying minors reported as possible. National corrections imposed care denial on trans inmates.
care_services.protection: No insurer or state-employee protections; no documented care-access protection for visitors.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing care for a minor, or seeking care in a state using public records, may be exposed to subpoena or denial. Care decisions can become investigation matters.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism framing names 'radically pro-transgender' groups as targets; cash-reward system; federal orders direct enforcement against schools. State SB79 frames gender as binary and immutable. State gender-identity exclusion treated as official policy.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Stated limit that counterterrorism will not target people who merely disagree; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-level threat framing and national security framing reinforce one another; visible trans people may be read as security subjects.

minors_guardians.exposure: Adult traveller with minor: care for minors is criminal for providers; facility bans cover minors in schools and public buildings; denial of care for accompanying minors reported; SB184 and national subpoenas of under-19 records.
minors_guardians.protection: Chaperoning and emergency exemptions in facility statute; no statewide protection for minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's transition-related needs or school-age exclusion put a guardian in direct exposure to state and federal enforcement.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence rate; the 3.8/100k figure is an undercount floor and is not used. No state hate-crime coverage for gender identity; ID-check friction reported for non-matching documents.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; two municipalities ban all discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to trans-specific violence is not documented for this state; partial recourse exists only at municipal level.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide public-accommodation recourse; appellate rulings upheld licence refusal; national passport policy rolled out; enforcement of the trespass statute unclear beyond one arrest; stated ID inconsistency may hit visitors through checks.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Ombuds-type and municipal remedies exist locally; national litigation is ongoing; some orders enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are unavailable where state law permits the exposure, and national courts are split on document rights.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both involve document-based refusal of visitors with universal application and weak remedy. This case adds facility exclusion, criminal trespass arrests and documented immigration custody abuse, which are more severe. It sits somewhat lower than 0.35-A for custody harm but without an exclusion register.

Closest match: birth-sex facility rules and arrests in government buildings, with housing or custody harm. The dossier shows documented custody abuse and minors' care criminalisation, which make it similar. It is slightly higher because the dossier has no documented birth-sex prison housing in this state and no documented state police raids.

Both involve universal registration-like exposure without lethal risk. This case is somewhat lower because of documented custody abuse, criminal trespass arrests, and minors' care criminalisation. It is comparable on remedy weakness.
Anchor 0.55-B has administrative denial with a remedy path and no custody abuse. This case has documented custody abuse, criminal trespass, and no statewide protection, so it sits clearly below.

parsed.synthesis: The national passport regime, refusal cable and immigration custody harms form a universal-exposure base that a state facility ban and trespass statute compound. The state adds birth-sex facility rules in government buildings, minors' care criminalisation and absent statewide protections. Municipal and national hate-crime recourse partly mitigates but is not shown working for visitors. Violence cannot be rated because the only figure is an undercount floor. The trespass arrest and immigration-custody abuses are documented exposures, and their interaction with document discrepancy is the principal chain of harm. The overall rating reflects documented tier-1 universal exposure and tier-2 state targeting, offset only partly by local remedies.
